fundamental.thesis: GMR Airports is India's largest private airport concessionaire, operating Delhi (DIAL, 78.7mn pax), Hyderabad (GHIAL, 30.5mn pax), and Goa-Mopa, with Bhogapuram greenfield (Visakhapatnam) targeting commissioning by Q2FY27 — revenue is a direct function of regulated aero tariffs × traffic plus non-aero commercial yields, making it a concession infrastructure story, not a conventional industrial. Revenue has accelerated materially — from +17.7% YoY in FY25 to +40.0% in FY26 (₹15,201 Cr) and +48.6% in Q3FY26 (₹4,083 Cr) — powered largely by a one-cycle Delhi aero tariff revision that drove 178% aero revenue growth; PAT turned positive for the first time in over a decade at ₹472 Cr (3.1% FY26 margin vs –7.5% FY25), but the trajectory is thin and uneven, with Q1FY26 still loss-making (–₹137 Cr), and EPS estimates have been revised down –11.5% over the past 90 days. At 25.4× trailing P/E vs the FMCG benchmark of 40–65×, the stock screens as cheap in nominal terms, but EV/EBITDA of 25× at P55 in the broad market (a slight premium to median) and extreme leverage (D/E: 21.3) signal the P/E discount is structural — earned by a commodity business model with 6.2% EBITDA margins, not by mispricing — and the classic pre-derating pattern (–13.8% EPS revisions over 90 days while all 4 analysts remain on Buy) warrants scepticism about the 44% consensus upside target. The biggest risk is the lethal combination of sustained palm oil input cost inflation (+35% YoY), near-zero FCF generation, and exceptionally high financial leverage, which leaves the company highly exposed to any demand or commodity disruption; the stock sitting at just 6.5% of its 52-week range suggests the market is already pricing in significant stress.
